name: Comp-Tool HUD — make compiler tools salient at decision-time
description: Andrew-direct 2026-06-15 (the 'agent HUD' question): catalog updates (CLAUDE.md / graph-call-manifest / comp-tools.yaml) are the discoverability FLOOR, but the real problem is SALIENCE-AT-DECISION-TIME -- agents blind-grep instead of reaching for the stronger repo-scoped comp-* tool, because grep is the zero-friction default reflex and the catalog is periphery the agent must choose to consult. Three arms (Andrew: do all three): #1 PreToolUse INTERCEPT HOOK (CTO) -- surface the right comp call via additionalContext the moment an agent Grep/Globs for a comp-answerable signature; ADVISORY (search still runs) + once-per-class-per-session dedupe (anti-noise) + logged; #2 `comp-which "<question>"` ROUTER (CTO) -- lower the which-tool friction so the agent asks its question and gets the canonical call without knowing the 41KB catalog; #3 MEASUREMENT (CVO) -- baseline the blind-grep-where-a-tool-exists rate + rank the buried tools + extract the high-confidence target patterns. Andrew's sequencing: CVO's #3 data tells CTO how to optimize #2 (build the router's question->tool map on what agents ACTUALLY ask, not a-priori guesses) + tunes #1's pattern set.
